goal: stronger README-area background and enclosing-frame illusion without claiming host-page overlay authority

segmented-frame.notes: Shared x=18/x=882 rails recur across bridge, Projects, Activity and footer. GitHub desktop/mobile rendering preserves readability and avoids host-table compression while producing a clearer repeated outer-frame grammar than envelope v3 and the first segmented prototype.

single-table-frame.notes: GitHub preserved the three-column enclosure, but host table borders/padding became visually dominant and mobile compressed the center content too aggressively. Preserve only as negative evidence.

font_portability.implementation: Japanese Projects/Activity SVG labels are deterministic vector outlines; generated and stable section bands reject SVG <text>.
font_portability.result: The same headless GitHub environment that previously showed tofu renders both section labels visibly on desktop and mobile.
font_portability.remaining_boundary: Host HTML text such as the copyright line still depends on the browser/OS font; this gate covers repository-owned SVG section labels only.

hard_boundaries: No claim of background/overlay outside the README rendering area.
Do not replace factual project/activity content with a flattened decorative mockup.
Do not promote the rejected table experiment.
Frame decoration must remain removable without breaking content authority or links.
The active bridge and shared rail chrome must switch atomically with the seasonal envelope.
A target-render PASS for layout does not imply that optional SMIL animation visibly plays.
Essential repository-owned non-Latin SVG labels must not regress to client-font-dependent <text>.
next_safe_action: Keep envelope v4 live, monitor the first scheduled Summer-to-Autumn switch on 2026-09-01, and continue treating public SMIL playback as a separate runtime gate.
